findings.F1: The 20-day move is followed by a same-direction excess 10-day return that grows with the coin's 20-day volatility relative to its own median. By volatility quintile (non-overlapping 10-day grid, cases of one day together) it rises from +0.26 % (t 0.25, 598 cases, 116 days) through +0.20 %, +0.87 % and +1.87 % (t 2.02) to +3.42 % (t 2.17, 597 cases, 172 days). The top quintile's excess is about 15 times the 0.22 % cost of a trade.
findings.F2: The same volatility gradient holds over 20 days, with excess returns from +0.15 % in the lowest volatility quintile to +7.14 % in the highest (t 1.32, 291 cases). It also holds across coins: in the high-volatility tercile the 10-day directional excess is positive for 15 of 19 coins (e.g. AVAX +7.6 %, t 2.60; SOL +4.7 %, t 2.08). By period it is +3.98 % (t 2.12) up to 2021 and +1.60 % (t 1.31) from 2022.
findings.F3: In the lowest volatility tercile the 20-day move predicts nothing over the next 10 days: directional excess −0.14 % (t −0.16, 995 cases). The whole tested effect (+1.06 %, t 1.52 overall) comes from the mid tercile (+1.35 %, t 1.84) and the high tercile (+2.76 %, t 2.48).
findings.F4: Inside the high-volatility tercile, the size of the 20-day move does not grade the continuation; the smallest moves carry the most. The 10-day directional excess is +3.98 % (t 3.00) for the smallest |z20| tercile, +2.87 % (t 1.76) for the middle one and +1.44 % (t 0.91) for the largest. So it is the direction of the recent move under high volatility that carries information, not its extremity.
findings.F5: The book's gain comes from its long side. Daily position gains summed to +33.2 on long days (mean +0.18 % a day, 18,092 coin-days) against −7.5 on short days (−0.04 % a day). Long trades averaged +10.6 % net against −2.5 % for short trades. Yet the excess continuation is the same for both sides (+1.06 %, t 1.03 after rises; +1.00 %, t 1.14 after falls), so the shorts' loss is the coins' upward drift, not a failed signal.
findings.F6: Other angles showed nothing that stands out once the number of tables (about 20) is counted:

ideas.idea: The higher a coin's volatility over the past 20 days relative to its own usual level, the further its price keeps moving in the direction of its 20-day return over the next 10 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader should lean with a coin's past-month direction mainly when its recent daily swings are unusually wide, and refuse to trade that direction when the coin has been unusually calm.
ideas.name: volatility-scaled monthly continuation

ideas.idea: When a coin's 20-day volatility is high relative to its usual level, the sign of its 20-day return predicts the next 10 days' move, and the more that volatility exceeds its usual level, the larger the same-direction move, whatever the size of the 20-day return.
ideas.consequence: In a turbulent coin a trader should follow the direction of the past month even after a modest move, rather than waiting for an extreme one.
ideas.name: direction not size, turbulent coins

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's 20-day return on the upside, combined with high 20-day volatility relative to its usual level, the more its price rises over the next 10 days. Gains after falls are mostly erased by the coin's upward drift.
ideas.consequence: A trader should take the continuation trade on the long side in volatile coins, and refuse to short a volatile coin's fall on this signal alone.
ideas.name: long-side volatile continuation
